findings.actual_call_path: In Minecraft 1.14.4 and 1.15–1.17.1 client binaries, Mojang-mapped com.mojang.realmsclient.client.FileDownload downloads the server-returned WorldDownload.downloadLink into a temporary backup.tar.gz, then untarGzipArchive constructs GzipCompressorInputStream and TarArchiveInputStream, calls getNextTarEntry, and copies each entry. The Realms API request route is worlds/{worldId}/slot/{slotId}/download. CFR 0.152 decompilation was checked against the exact Mojang client artifact and mappings for 1.14.4 and 1.17.1; the pinned client constant-pool scan records matching caller classes for all applicable versions.
findings.effective_configuration: This route is reached through the optional, user-initiated Realms world-download screen; it is not a background parse on ordinary client startup. The URL and archive response are supplied through the Realms API/download flow. The service-generated tar metadata and a hostile Realm member’s ability to control exploit-specific header fields were not established.
findings.reachability_finding: The vulnerable TAR parser path is present and receives network-downloaded Realms backup bytes in the exact affected client versions 1.14.4, 1.15–1.17.1. The affected library is 1.8.1. This confirms component reachability behind an explicit download action, but the exploit precondition—attacker control of a malformed TAR entry with the inconsistent lengths needed for CVE-2021-35517—remains unverified. In 1.14.0–1.14.3 the package is affected but no direct TarArchiveInputStream reference was found.
findings.verified_mitigation: No mod-controlled mitigation was identified. The game owns Commons Compress; the mod does not declare or bundle this library and no runtime override was made.
findings.compatible_remediation: The authoritative advisory lists Commons Compress 1.21 as first patched for this package range. Minecraft versions with the affected 1.8.1 manifest need a game-side, compatibility-tested library update; no mod-side override is supported.
findings.remaining_uncertainty: The Realm server creates the archive. No controlled experiment established whether a Realm owner can cause server output to contain the malformed TAR metadata required by the advisory. No end-to-end Realms backup test or isolated CVE reproducer against 1.8.1 and 1.21 was run. The tar extraction destination also uses entry names to construct paths; path normalization and archive-entry control need separate security review.
findings.confidence: High for exact package/source versions and the observed vanilla client class references; high for the 1.14.4/1.17.1 mapped call chain; low for attacker control of the server-generated TAR header and resulting exploitability.
findings.responsible_owner: skyRolly (project security decision) and Mojang (game-managed runtime dependency and Realms client path)
findings.reviewer: Codex automated technical investigation; independent human review pending
follow_up_requirements: Establish, using a safe mock or Mojang-supplied test Realm, whether a Realm owner can control the TAR size/length fields that trigger CVE-2021-35517.
Reproduce the upstream TAR DoS with exact Commons Compress 1.8.1 under a resource-limited isolated process, and compare with fixed 1.21.
Review the Realms TAR entry extraction path for traversal and enforce normalized containment upstream if vulnerable.
Request Mojang to update the game-owned Commons Compress runtime on affected versions; do not override it in this mod.

build_gradle_control_assessment.method: Read build.gradle by exact source commit through GitHub file API and recorded the returned Git blob SHA plus direct dependency declarations.
build_gradle_control_assessment.result: No source group directly declares Commons Compress, Netty, Log4j, LZ4, Jackson, Guava, or Apache Commons dependencies. The only dependency declarations are the Minecraft game artifact and Fabric Loader. This does not inspect the Loom/Gradle plugin transitive classpaths; the advisory scopes in this investigation bind to Minecraft runtime manifests.
